name: Wald Family Foods
old_description: As part of our efforts to stay involved in causes that are important to our team members, Wald Family Foods has been a proud sponsor of the Coaches vs. Cancer (CvC) Las Vegas Golf Classic since 2021. The CvC program is a nationwide collaboration between the American Cancer Society and the National Association of Basketball Coaches.
about:
Wald Family Foods operates from McPherson, Kansas, where it has built a food manufacturing business over more than 25 years. The company's name reflects its family ownership, though founders are not publicly named. It began as a partner for brands seeking custom food production, evolving into a multi-facility operation.

The company runs five food facilities equipped for private-label and custom manufacturing. Its capabilities span sauce production using a Graco Saniforce cold-blend mixing system and a 3-head Grote spot sauce applicator, kettle cooking for enchilada, burrito, and quesadilla fillings, spiral freezing, and a dual chill bath that drops product temperature below 55°F in under 50 minutes. A cold-press crust line produces 90–100 crusts per minute, supported by three production lines—two laminated sheeting lines and one doughball line. Wald Family Foods handles on-site test runs, full line production, and product fulfillment for soups, pasta, Mexican-style dishes, and other frozen items sold under its Taste Traditions brand.

Customers include national retailers such as Albertsons, ALDI, Costco, Hy-Vee, and distributors like Ben E. Keith, as well as brands like Bernatello's, Conagra Brands, Nestlé, and Schwan's. The company serves retail, food-service, restaurant, healthcare, education, hospitality, military, and business-and-industry channels, offering both private-label development and ready-to-use retail and food-service products.

Wald Family Foods emphasizes flexibility and brand integrity, promising never to put a label on a product that doesn't represent the customer's brand. Its Waldsafe program—"Safe People. Safe Facilities. Safe Food."—drives a company-wide safety culture. Community involvement includes sponsoring the Coaches vs. Cancer Las Vegas Golf Classic since 2021.

about:
Walton Plastics, Inc. operates from Walton Hills, Ohio, a suburb southeast of Cleveland. The company was founded in 1992 and has remained under family ownership since its inception, a structure the firm says keeps customer needs at the center of its decisions.

The company produces rigid and flexible PVC (vinyl) sheet as well as thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) sheet through extrusion. It runs three manufacturing facilities, the most recent added to expand capacity and secure supply chains. In-house capabilities include in-line lamination for acrylic cap layers, decorative films, and reinforcement fabrics, plus a physical testing laboratory that certifies color, impact resistance, and dimensional accuracy. Custom formulation development is offered for specialized applications.

Walton Plastics serves markets that include building products (wall panels, trim), electrical enclosures, printing and graphics substrates, thermoforming feedstock, and engineered materials for custom applications. Customers range from fabricators and OEMs to distributors seeking tailored sheet properties such as weatherability, printability, or specific mechanical performance.

The firm emphasizes its family-owned culture as a driver of responsive service and technical competence. It points to plant-wide quality initiatives, advanced PVC production expertise, and the ability to laminate and test in-house as factors that differentiate it from competitors. The recent facility expansion was undertaken specifically to give customers added supply-chain assurance.

name: Warrior Energy
old_description: Warrior Energy, LLC (WEL) specializes in general contracting program management services, electrical installations, instrumentation and controls installations, and related services for industrial, government, oilfield/energy, institutional, commercial, and municipal facility projects.
about:
Warrior Energy, LLC was established in 2019 in Devils Lake, North Dakota, as a Native American–owned, SBA-certified small disadvantaged business. The company operates as a limited liability company and has expanded to include a branch in Grand Forks. Leadership includes President/COO Scott Schmaltz and General Manager/CEO Darin Hultberg, among a team of project managers and trade foremen.

The firm provides multi-discipline general contracting and program management, self-performing electrical construction (high/low voltage wiring, cable tray, switchgear, fiber optics), instrumentation and control services (calibration, loop checks, PLC/DCS panel installation), HVAC maintenance and controls, welding fabrication (structural stands, skids, platforms), roustabout and pipeline services (facility construction, flowline excavation, welding, backfill), insulation (fiberglass, jacketing, removable blankets), and coating/painting. Bonding capacity is $500,000 per project with a $1,000,000 aggregate.

Warrior Energy serves industrial, government, oilfield/energy, institutional, commercial, and municipal facility owners. Typical projects include new construction, retrofits, emergency repairs, and planned maintenance for clients such as energy producers, public agencies, and commercial developers.

The company emphasizes a full-service approach that covers pre-construction planning, design, engineering, coordination, and project management, backed by 24-hour emergency response. Its core values—service, quality, and integrity—are framed around adaptability, attention to detail, and transparent accountability.

name: Watersong Custom Furniture
old_description: The table on the right is done in white Maple, at 8 feet long and 18″ high, is a very low unit in this green house turned meditation space. It’s custom size is particular both to its use and its space, as it needs to be accessible to the occupant of the low bench immediately adjacent, and fit the available spot....
about:
Watersong Custom Furniture operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where owner Andy has run the business as a sole proprietor for over four decades. Andy’s woodworking roots trace back to childhood in Africa, where he observed utilitarian woodcraft, and later in Italy, where he encountered elaborate carved furniture. Those experiences shaped a philosophy that values quality, craftsmanship, and durability. The shop has remained at the same location since its inception, a 1,500‑square‑foot space divided between a small showroom and a working area with a finishing booth.

The company produces one‑of‑a‑kind residential furniture including tables, entertainment centers, headboards, beds, dressers, display cases, desks, bookshelves, cabinetry, benches, and vanities. Every piece is designed and built by Andy alone, from hand‑selecting lumber to final delivery. He works primarily in domestic hardwoods such as ash, cherry, hickory, maple, oak, pine, poplar, and walnut, supplemented by exotic species like purple heart, padauk, zebra wood, wenge, and mahogany for accents. Joinery is screwed and glued rather than stapled, and hardware consists of European hinges and steel ball‑bearing slides. A water‑based finish option is available for environmentally sensitive clients.

Watersong serves homeowners and individual clients seeking custom pieces that fit unique spaces and functional needs. Examples from the portfolio include a low maple table for a meditation room, a built‑in vanity with dual sinks and a cedar‑lined hamper, and entertainment centers designed to adapt to evolving technology. The business does not target commercial or institutional markets; its customer base is residential.

Andy emphasizes that the sole‑proprietor model ensures a single point of accountability from design through delivery, eliminating the “too many cooks” problem. The company’s differentiators are its four‑decade tenure at one address, hand‑selected materials, premium hardware, and a willingness to ship finished pieces across the country—from Wyoming to Texas and California to New Jersey.

name: Waxoyl USA
old_description: Trusted by specialists the world over, Waxoyl Professional makes customized solutions to retain value and the like-new qualities of all types of transportation, machinery and structures.
about:
Waxoyl USA operates from Westford, Vermont, where it was founded in 1971. The company specializes in corrosion protection solutions for transportation, machinery, and structures, drawing on more than five decades of experience in the field.

The product line centers on three main coatings: Hardwax, a tough, flexible wax-based barrier for underbody protection; Professional 120-4, a cavity fogging treatment that penetrates seams and displaces moisture; and Hardwax21, formulated for maximum abrasion resistance in extreme environments. All products are supplied in kegs, tins, and aerosol cans alongside a range of professional application tools designed to reach cavities without drilling.

The coatings are used by original equipment manufacturers across automotive, commercial vehicle, and rail sectors, including car, bus, and truck makers, vehicle importers, pre-delivery inspection centers, train builders, and heavy earth-moving equipment producers. Specialists worldwide apply the system to protect bridges, fleet vehicles, and industrial structures.

Waxoyl emphasizes that a single application of 120-4 can protect for the life of a vehicle, with active protection spanning -40°F to 300°F. The coatings are safe on paint, rubber, and electrical components, and they stop existing surface rust while lubricating moving parts such as window tracks. Touch-ups are needed only where the coating has been physically abraded.

name: Weavetec Inc
old_description: Weavetec, Inc. is a specialty weaver owned and managed by the Pennington family that has operated in Upstate South Carolina since 1987.
about:
Weavetec, Inc. was founded in 1987 by the Pennington family in Blacksburg, South Carolina, in the Upstate region. The company remains family-owned and managed, drawing on over 90 years of textile industry experience across generations. Harold Pennington Jr. serves as vice president, while Andrew Pennington oversees sales and operations, and Laurinda Pennington manages customer service.

The firm operates as a specialty weaver producing custom woven fabrics for industrial and home furnishing markets. Its capabilities include sectional warping on Benninger warpers, dobby weaving on looms of varying widths and harness counts, and jacquard weaving configured around a standard 54‑inch width. In‑house throw finishing provides washing, drying, cutting, folding, and sewing for blankets and tapestries. The plant employs approximately 200 people.

Weavetec serves the upholstery fabric industry, manufacturers of woven throws and tapestry blankets, and broader industrial textile applications. Customers range from brands seeking multicolor tapestry blankets to companies needing durable upholstery materials and specialty fabrics for niche uses.

The company emphasizes construction flexibility, a reputation for responsive customer service, and product value, all framed by a mission to produce Made‑in‑USA textiles with integrity and precision. In‑house finishing and a family‑management structure are cited as key differentiators.
